description: Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU), NSF NHERI 2024: Tensile Behavior of Unsaturated Soil via Beam Bending Tests is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Jose Ortiz Michel, University of California Davis (ucdavis.edu). This project investigates the tensile behavior of unsaturated compacted soil using a three-point beam bending test. This approach aims to evaluate the tensile strength of soil, which is important for understanding crack propagation in levees and earthen dams due to fault movements, particularly vertical fault displacement. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project with 3 top-level files (PDF). Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-0bf8-e592. Keywords: NSF NHERI Center for Geotechnical Modeling, Tensile behavior, compacted unsaturated soil, embankment cracking. Published 2024-10-02. Facility named: Center for Geotechnical Modeling - University of California, Davis. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
